sections.title: The pattern you already know
sections.content: You know the subjunctive after *aconsejar que* from B1 Unit 4 (*Te recomiendo que hables con tu profesor*) and after reported orders such as *prohibir* from B1 Unit 38 (*Nos prohibió que saliéramos de noche*). The logic is the same for every verb of influence: the main verb tries to get someone else to act, so the action after *que* has not happened yet and goes in the subjunctive. At B2 you use the whole range, from gentle to strong.

sections.title: From gentle to strong
rows: pedir que, aconsejar que, recomendar que

sections.title: Which tense?
sections.content: As you saw in B1 Unit 38, the tense follows the main verb. A present main verb takes the present subjunctive; a past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive. You know both the *-ra* and the *-se* forms from B1 Unit 4.

sections.title: The same demand in two tenses
rows: La jefa exige que lleguemos a las nueve.
The boss demands that we arrive at nine.
La jefa exigió que llegáramos a las nueve.
The boss demanded that we arrive at nine.

items.spanish: El director prohibió que usáramos el móvil durante la reunión.
items.english: The director forbade us to use our phones during the meeting.

items.spanish: Mis padres no permitían que volviéramos tarde a casa.
items.english: My parents did not allow us to come home late.

items.spanish: El mal tiempo impidió que el avión saliera a la hora.
items.english: The bad weather stopped the plane from leaving on time.

items.spanish: Los vecinos insistieron en que cenáramos con ellos.
items.english: The neighbours insisted that we have dinner with them.

sections.content: There are always two people: the one who demands and the one who has to act. *Insistir* needs *en*: *insistir en que*. When the person who demands and the person who acts are the same, Spanish uses an infinitive instead (Lesson 4 of this unit).
